newsitem.title: MEXICO: Serfin comes back from the brink in Q2.
newsitem.headline: Serfin comes back from the brink in Q2.

text.p: Grupo Financiero Serfin took a positive step back to healthy banking in the second quarter after years of struggling with a legacy of unsound loans.
In its second quarter earnings report, the banking group reported a net profit of 89 million pesos, building on net income of 46 million pesos in the first quarter.
Those profits were a drop in the ocean compared to staggering losses of some 7 billion pesos in 1996, and were bolstered by some 80 million pesos of deferred tax credits in the second quarter.
But its banking unit Banca Serfin attracted deposits and improved asset quality in the quarter, giving banking analysts hope of a sounder future.
"They're turning the bank around, and at this point we can be pretty confident it will survive," said Carlos Gomez of Paribas in New York. "A year ago we couldn't be sure."

The biggest plus was a 19.8 percent surge in core deposits over the first quarter, partly the result of successful marketing of its new "Maxicuenta" product that showed the bank was attracting customers and shedding the stigma of crisis that had kept new clients away.
While deposits were scarce, the bank had been forced to fund itself in the money markets -- the most expensive form of borrowing.

In the second quarter, low-yielding average core deposits represented 25 percent of total deposits up from 21 percent in the first quarter, and its net interest margin edged up to 3.2 percent from 3.1 percent over the same period.

On the asset side, past-due loans fell by 5.5 percent, excluding write-offs, from the first quarter, which analysts said was a positive trend that is unlikely to be shared by two of Serfin's bigger rivals, Banamex and Bancomer, because they retain rafts of troubled mortgage loans on their books.
Last year, Serfin sold the bulk of its mortgage portfolio to the government in exchange for a full-scale restructuring and recapitalization effort.
In a conference call to analysts on Tuesday, Serfin CEO Alfredo Lagos said the bank was trying to "shrink" in size, or reduce its portfolio of outstanding loans.
Analysts said its commercial lending fell some 15 percent in the quarter over the first -- a worrying trend if it continues, but understandable for the time being.
But they were encouraged by an impressive 133 million pesos of recoveries in the second quarter -- renewed payments on loans that had previously been written off.

"In very general terms, (the report) does suggest good news at least in the sense that non-performing loans are going in the right direction. Asset quality is bottoming out," said Robert Lacoursiere, analyst at Santander Investments in Mexico.

He noted, however, that the bank has put many non-performing loans in the restructuring category, which he said under standard accounting practices was not a guarantee they would become current until there had been several consecutive payments.
Serfin's share price in the Mexican market rose 7 centavos at Tuesday's close to 2.70 after the results, while its ADR was down a cent to 3.01.
Profits per peso share in second quarter were 4 centavos, up from 2 centavos in the first quarter. Earnings per ADR were $0.02, up from $0.01.
Both shares trade very differently, and the ADR is considered far more expensive in terms of price to book value than its peso counterpart.
Analysts were unlikely to raise recommendations on the stock, given that some $300 million of a capitalization plan is still to be completed, and that could further dilute shares.
Also, they put the profits in perspective. "Although they're improving and the figures are in the black, we're not seeing huge profitability," noted Carole Milnes, analyst at Abaco brokerage.
Paribas' Gomez pointed out that the bank created only 9 million pesos of new reserves in the second quarter.
"The bank is breaking even because of tax credits and it is not making provisions," he said. "Under normal conditions, it should be creating reserves."
((-- Mexico City newsroom +525 728-9560))
